items.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022
items.q: I was mentioning this to Mr. Domenico today, we just had a cup of coffee before coming over here

ctx.x: Yeah I commented to someone as we were going out the door I said, “I bet you didn’t expect the night was going to end like that.” It was terrific. Audience communication. And I think you — it’s obvious you learned from your father and maybe even from the Stones like about the entertainment factor involved in presenting music. I saw it.

Well I mean I try my best not to be like — you hate to say — well like you said you know one of the great ballads, “Willow Weep for Me” to the Stones’ that’s one of the most famous songs ever, “Satisfaction” has been covered by everyone from Aretha Franklin to Stevie Wonder to — well it’s just so famous, to the “Beer Barrel Polka” — everyone who knows a polka that’s probably the most well known polka. So it’s almost like I’m trying not to make it too kitsch or too like I’m not trying to go like you know ultra…

went to Romania to play a gig at this really cool venue, small place, and it was such a nice night we moved it out to the back deck because it was a full moon, perfect weather, about a hundred people sitting, it was ultra quiet it was like you could hear a pin drop. And people were so — it was a totally acoustic, no amplification, acoustic bass, acoustic piano, acoustic drums and it was like the connection with the audience with this beautiful night and all the people afterwards, we hung for hours talking to the…
